chunks.text: Today, we will talk about Zimbabwe.
Zimbabwe is a beautiful, landlocked, and historic country in Southern Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Zimbabwe?
Zimbabwe is in Southern Africa.
It is next to Zambia, Mozambique, South Africa, and Botswana.
It has no ocean, but it has rivers, lakes, and mountains.
The Zambezi River forms the border with Zambia.
What is the capital city of Zimbabwe?
The capital city is Harare.
Harare is in the northeast of the country.
It has offices, schools, markets, and parks.
It is the largest city in Zimbabwe.
Other cities include Bulawayo in the South, full of culture and history.
Mutare near the mountains and the Mozambique border.
Victoria Falls, a small city near the famous waterfall.
How many people live in Zimbabwe?
About 16 million people live in Zimbabwe.
Many live in cities, but many others live in villages and farming areas.
Zimbabwe has many ethnic groups, including the Shona and Debele people.
What language do people speak in Zimbabwe?
Zimbabwe has 16 official languages.
The most widely spoken are Shona and Debele English, used in schools, business, and government.
Many people speak two or three languages every day.
What is the weather like in Zimbabwe?
Zimbabwe has a mild tropical climate, rainy season from November to March, dry season from April to October, warm summers and cool winters, especially in the highlands.
It is good weather for farming and tourism.
What does Zimbabwe look like?
Zimbabwe has mountains and green hills, rivers, like the Zambezi and Limpopo Lake Cariba, one of the biggest lakes in Africa, forests, grasslands, and national parks.
It is also home to Victoria Falls, one of the biggest waterfalls in the world.
What animals live in Zimbabwe?
Zimbabwe has many wild animals such as elephants, lions, and rhinos, leopards, giraffes, and buffalo, hippos and crocodiles in the rivers, zebras, wildebeest, and many birds.
Many people go to Zimbabwe for safari and nature travel.
What do people eat in Zimbabwe?
Zimbabwean food is simple, filling, and often homemade.
People eat sardza, thick maize porridge, eaten every day.
Vegetables like kale, pumpkin leaves, and spinach, beans, peanuts, and sweet potatoes.
Chicken, beef, and fish.
Popular dishes, sardza with relish, meat, or vegetables and sauce.
Kapenta, small dried fish.
Mahu, a thick fermented maize drink.
Maputi, puffed maize like popcorn.
What do people drink in Zimbabwe?
People drink water, tea, and herbal drinks.
Mahu, traditional maize drink.
Milk and fruit juice.
Adults may drink local beer or chibuku.
People often share drinks with friends and family.
What is life like in Zimbabwe?
Life in Zimbabwe is often peaceful, family -based, and community -focused.
People enjoy farming, teaching, or working in shops.
Spending time with family, going to school and church, singing, dancing, and playing drums.
Watching football, a popular sport.
Many people live close to nature and follow traditional customs.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, April 18th.
Heroes Day and Defense Forces Day in August.
Christmas and Easter, harvest festivals and family gatherings.
Traditional weddings with music, food, and special clothes.
People love to celebrate with singing, dancing, and sharing meals.
Some fun facts about Zimbabwe.
Victoria Falls is also called the Smoke That Thunders.
Great Zimbabwe is an ancient stone city built over 700 years ago.
The flag has green, gold, red, black, and a white triangle with a red star and a bird.
Zimbabwe has no ocean, but it has beautiful lakes and rivers.
The currency is now mostly US dollars or Zimbabwe in bond notes.
Now you know many things about Zimbabwe.
You know where it is, what people eat, and how they live.
You learned about Victoria Falls, SADZA, and the friendly people.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English podcast.
I am Emily.
See you next time.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Shona, Sarudzai Zvakanaka.
That means stay well.
